cards.title: Remember observable state across recomposition
cards.body: Guidance: Remember an object with remember; its initial value is stored in the Composition and reused during recomposition. Wrap changing UI data in mutableStateOf so changes to value schedule recomposition of composables that read it. For example, remember { mutableStateOf("") } retains an editable name while the UI recomposes. Limitation: remember does not retain state across configuration changes; use rememberSaveable for state that must survive them.

cards.title: Hoist shared state and pass events upward
cards.body: Guidance: Move state to a caller and pass the current value plus an event callback, such as value and onValueChange. This keeps one source of truth while callers can accept, change, or ignore events. Hoist to at least the lowest common parent of readers and the highest level that writes the state. States changed by the same events should be hoisted together. Limitation: merely exposing callbacks is insufficient if the state owner remains below a reader or writer; underhoisting prevents the intended downward-state, upward-event flow.

cards.title: Save only the UI state needed for restoration
cards.body: Guidance: Use rememberSaveable for UI state owned by a composable or a Composition-scoped state holder when it must survive activity or process recreation. Primitive values are saved automatically; custom types can use Parcelize, listSaver, mapSaver, or a custom Saver. Limitation: saved UI state shares a size-limited Bundle with other saved-instance-state APIs. Store minimal IDs or keys and rebuild complex state through persistent storage instead of putting large objects or object lists in the Bundle.

cards.title: Tie suspend work to LaunchedEffect keys
cards.body: Guidance: Use LaunchedEffect for suspend work that belongs to a composable lifetime. It launches its coroutine when entering the Composition and cancels it on leaving. Choose keys that identify when the work must restart: a changed key cancels the existing coroutine and starts a new one. For example, keying a repeating pulse by pulseRateMs restarts the delay-and-animation loop when the rate changes. Limitation: work is cancelled on key changes or removal, so its lifetime is governed by that effect call and its keys.

cards.title: Read the latest callback without restarting an effect
cards.body: Guidance: Use rememberUpdatedState when a long-lived effect must capture a changing callback or value without restarting its work. Read the returned State inside the effect. In a timeout screen, rememberUpdatedState(onTimeout) lets a LaunchedEffect(true) finish its existing delay and then invoke the latest callback. A constant key makes the effect match the call-site lifetime. Limitation: pass a changing value as an effect key when it should restart the effect; the updated-state approach is for values whose changes should not restart it.

cards.title: Register and clean up subscriptions with DisposableEffect
cards.body: Guidance: Use DisposableEffect when a side effect needs cleanup after a key changes or the composable leaves the Composition. Register the observer or resource inside the effect and undo registration in onDispose. Keying a lifecycle observer by lifecycleOwner removes the old observer and registers against the new owner when it changes. rememberUpdatedState can keep observer callbacks current. Limitation: onDispose must be the final statement of the effect block; changing keys disposes and recreates the effect.

cards.title: Use derivedStateOf when UI changes less often than inputs
cards.body: Guidance: Use derivedStateOf when state changes more frequently than the UI needs to update, such as a scroll position whose UI only reacts after crossing a threshold. Observe the derived state so the consumer responds to meaningful result changes, similarly to distinctUntilChanged. Limitation: combining state values is not itself a reason to use derivedStateOf. A full name made from firstName and lastName must change whenever either input changes, so ordinary string composition is enough and derivedStateOf adds unnecessary overhead.

cards.title: Convert external data to Compose State with produceState
cards.body: Guidance: Use produceState to expose external data as Compose State. Its producer coroutine starts on entering the Composition, updates the returned state through value, and is cancelled on leaving. Supply inputs as keys when changed inputs should cancel and relaunch the producer, as with a URL and image repository. For non-suspending subscriptions, use awaitDispose to remove the subscription. Limitation: the returned State conflates equal values; assigning the same value does not trigger recomposition.

cards.title: Observe Compose state as a cold Flow
cards.body: Guidance: Use snapshotFlow to turn reads of Compose State into a cold Flow. Its block runs when collected, and changes to state read by that block emit a new result only when it differs from the previous emitted value. Apply Flow operators for downstream behavior: map a list index to index > 0, then distinctUntilChanged and filter to record crossing the first-item threshold. Limitation: emission equality is checked on the block result; after mapping several distinct indices to the same boolean, use downstream distinctUntilChanged for that boolean.

cards.title: Choose modifier order to control the clickable area
cards.body: Guidance: Modifier order changes behavior because each modifier operates on the result of the preceding one. Use Modifier.clickable(...).padding(...) when the padded surrounding area should respond to clicks. Reverse the order to Modifier.padding(...).clickable(...) when the added padding should remain outside the clickable area. Limitation: the same modifier functions in a different sequence do not produce equivalent input behavior; assess the intended hit area when arranging the chain.

cards.title: Keep lazy item state attached to stable keys
cards.body: Guidance: Provide a stable, unique key such as message.id to lazy items when data can reorder. The default uses item position, so moving an item can lose remembered state; explicit keys let Compose move that state with the item. This also matters for a nested LazyRow whose scroll state should follow its row. Limitation: keys must use Bundle-supported types, such as primitives, enums, or Parcelables, so rememberSaveable state inside an item can be restored after activity recreation or scrolling away and back.

cards.title: Choose a gesture abstraction and key custom handlers
cards.body: Guidance: Use the highest gesture abstraction that supports the interaction: a component such as Button, then a gesture modifier such as clickable, then pointerInput for custom gestures. Higher layers include more semantics for accessibility. A pointerInput handler can await raw events with awaitPointerEventScope and awaitPointerEvent; pass keys for inputs whose changes should re-execute the handler. Limitation: raw event handling is complex and carries less semantic information than the higher-level component or gesture modifier.

cards.title: Keep TextField state and edit it after initialization
cards.body: Guidance: For a state-based TextField, use TextFieldState to own text content and selection, and hoist it where the architecture needs it. rememberTextFieldState remembers the state object and provides save/restore support. Pass it to TextField(state = ...); initialText and initialSelection establish initial content and selection. Limitation: changing the initial value passed to rememberTextFieldState during a later recomposition does not update the existing state. Use TextFieldState edit methods to change it after initialization.

cards.title: Draw with Canvas and DrawScope coordinates
cards.body: Guidance: Use drawing modifiers for custom rendering, or Canvas when the composable primarily draws. Canvas wraps Modifier.drawBehind, and drawing modifiers expose DrawScope with drawing functions and the current size. Use that size to position shapes within the drawing area. The origin is its top-left pixel: x increases rightward and y downward. Limitation: defaults on many draw methods place content at [0, 0] and fill the drawing area; provide positions and sizes when the desired geometry differs.

cards.title: Cache drawing objects with drawWithCache
cards.body: Guidance: Create reusable drawing objects such as Brush, Shader, or Path inside drawWithCache to avoid reallocating them on each draw. For example, create a gradient Brush in the cache block and draw with it from onDrawBehind. Objects used only for drawing can be cached here even where composition-based remember is unavailable. Limitation: this cache depends on the drawing area size and state read by the cache block; it is not a permanent cache across changes to those inputs.

cards.title: Coordinate exit animations before removing content
cards.body: Guidance: Use AnimatedVisibility to animate content appearing and disappearing; customize enter and exit transitions and combine them with +. To add custom animation that must finish before removal, attach it to the transition exposed inside the AnimatedVisibility content lambda. AnimatedVisibility waits for animations on that Transition before removing content. Limitation: independently created exit animations, such as animate*AsState, are not tracked by that Transition, so the content may be removed before they finish.

cards.title: Apply Scaffold content padding to the content root
cards.body: Guidance: Use Scaffold to assemble a Material screen from slots such as topBar, bottomBar, and floatingActionButton. Its content lambda receives PaddingValues that should be applied to the content root to constrain its size. A typical pattern is Scaffold(...) { innerPadding -> Column(Modifier.padding(innerPadding)) { ... } }. Limitation: supplying bars to Scaffold does not replace applying the padding passed to the content lambda; the documented example explicitly applies it to the Column.

cards.title: Merge semantics for a logical interactive element
cards.body: Guidance: Use Modifier.semantics(mergeDescendants = true) when descendant content should be understood as one logical element. A Button containing an icon and text is represented as a single merged leaf in the semantics tree. clickable and toggleable already request descendant merging, as does ListItem. Limitation: the semantics tree only includes nodes with semantic information; it is not a copy of every composable in the UI tree. Check whether the component already merges descendants before adding another merging rule.

cards.title: Synchronize Compose assertions and wait for external work
cards.body: Guidance: Compose test-rule actions and assertions synchronize with the UI before running, waiting for the UI tree to become idle and advancing a virtual clock. A plain assertion immediately after changing state can observe stale composition results; use a synchronized Compose assertion. For conditions depending on external work, such as data loading or Android measure/draw outside Compose, use waitUntil with a timeout and condition. Limitation: Compose hierarchy synchronization does not automatically cover the rest of the app.

cards.title: Read frequently changing state in layout or draw
cards.body: Guidance: When a changing value only affects placement, read it in a layout lambda such as Modifier.offset { IntOffset(0, scrollProvider()) }. The documented scroll example can then skip composition and update layout directly. If only a drawn color changes, read it inside drawBehind and drawRect so the update can skip composition and layout. Limitation: simply passing a lambda is not enough if you call it during composition; place the state read inside the layout or draw callback for the phase that needs it.

cards.title: Replace custom-control semantics deliberately
cards.body: Guidance: Use clearAndSetSemantics to replace a component and its descendants with semantics that describe the actual control. A custom toggle can supply stateDescription, toggleableState, and Role.Switch so accessibility services announce its state and toggle action. Limitation: an empty lambda removes that information from accessibility, autofill, and testing consumers. Use clearing only when needed, and consider modifier order: it clears semantics after its position regardless of other merging strategies.

cards.title: Measure text before sizing its drawn background
cards.body: Guidance: For manually drawn text, use rememberTextMeasurer and drawText. Measure with the intended constraints and TextStyle, then use the measured size for a matching background rectangle before drawing the text result. This accounts for text-specific sizing factors such as font size, ligatures, and letter spacing. Limitation: changing constraints, font size, or other measurement-affecting properties changes the reported size. Fixed width and height can be paired with TextOverflow.Ellipsis to constrain displayed text.

cards.title: Account for tap gesture consumption and cancellation
cards.body: Guidance: detectTapGestures consumes the first pointer down and final pointer up; after detecting a long press it consumes subsequent changes. If another handler already consumed the first down, the entire gesture, including onPress, is skipped. After onPress, leaving the input area or consumption of movement, down, or up can cancel recognition, so onTap, onDoubleTap, and onLongPress are not called afterward. Limitation: callback offsets can fall outside element bounds when the touch target is expanded to the minimum target size.

cards.title: Apply font weight to whole text or individual spans
cards.body: Guidance: Set Text fontWeight to FontWeight.Bold, or another FontWeight, to style its text. For different styles within one Text, build an AnnotatedString and wrap selected appended ranges with withStyle(SpanStyle(...)); the example makes one letter bold and red while leaving surrounding letters outside that span. TextStyle is for Text, while SpanStyle and ParagraphStyle belong in AnnotatedString. Limitation: use SpanStyle for inline ranges and ParagraphStyle for paragraph properties such as alignment, direction, line height, and indent.

cards.title: Animate a float toward changing targets
cards.body: Guidance: Use animateFloatAsState for a single animated float: supply the target and read the returned animation value, such as an alpha changing between 1f and 0.5f. The first target becomes the initial value; later target changes start animation automatically. If a target changes during animation, it continues toward the new target from the current value and velocity. Customize timing with an AnimationSpec. Limitation: this API animates one value; other data types need a corresponding animate*AsState API or animateValueAsState with a TwoWayConverter.

cards.title: Describe meaningful images and omit decorative descriptions
cards.body: Guidance: Provide Image and Icon with a textual contentDescription that explains a meaningful graphic; the framework cannot infer what the image displays. Use a localized string because this description is presented to users, as with a share icon labeled from string resources. Set contentDescription = null for a purely decorative graphic with no semantic meaning. Limitation: contentDescription is mainly for graphic elements; Text, Button, clickable, and toggleable already provide semantics for their intrinsic behavior.

cards.title: Combine drawing transforms inside Foundation Canvas
cards.body: Guidance: Use the Foundation Canvas composable when you need a layout element devoted to custom drawing; it wraps Modifier.drawBehind and exposes DrawScope drawing operations. Inside its drawing block, use withTransform to combine changes such as translation and rotation before issuing drawRect. This combines transformations in one operation instead of calculating and saving separately nested transformations. Limitation: place the drawing commands inside the withTransform content block to draw them with that combined transformation, as in the translated and rotated rectangle example.

cards.title: Feed value-based text fields from caller-owned state
cards.body: Guidance: For a value-based TextField, pass the current input text through value and handle updated text from onValueChange. Keep the value in observable caller-owned state and update that state in the callback, as the guide demonstrates with remember { mutableStateOf("") } and OutlinedTextField(value = name, onValueChange = { name = it }). Reads of that state schedule recomposition when it changes. Limitation: use the TextFieldValue overload if you also need to observe cursor location, selection, or IME composition; the String value represents input text.

cards.title: Place padding inside or outside the clickable area
cards.body: Guidance: Place padding after clickable when the surrounding padded space should respond to clicks: Modifier.clickable(...).padding(16.dp). Place padding before clickable when that added space should remain outside the clickable area: Modifier.padding(16.dp).clickable(...). Each modifier changes the result of the preceding modifier, so order determines the final input behavior. Limitation: equal padding values do not imply equal clickable areas; reversing these two modifiers changes whether the padded space reacts to input.

cards.title: Give Animatable an explicit starting value
cards.body: Guidance: Remember an Animatable when the first visible value should differ from the first animation target, for example a gray color that immediately animates to a status color. Call animateTo from a coroutine such as LaunchedEffect(status). A new target interrupts the animation and continues from its current value. Limitation: animateTo is suspending and needs a coroutine scope; continuous velocity across interruption is guaranteed for spring animations, so do not assume every animationSpec offers that guarantee.

cards.title: Sequence animations with suspending calls
cards.body: Guidance: To run animations one after another, call Animatable.animateTo sequentially in one coroutine: alpha.animateTo(1f), then offset.animateTo(100f). Each call suspends until that animation finishes before the next starts. Limitation: moving each call into launch changes the ordering to concurrent execution; interruption can also cancel the coroutine before later steps run.

cards.title: Launch independent Animatable values concurrently
cards.body: Guidance: To animate independent values at the same time, launch one child coroutine per Animatable inside the same effect or coroutine scope, for example launch { alpha.animateTo(1f) } and launch { offset.animateTo(100f) }. Limitation: consecutive animateTo calls without launch run sequentially; launching two animations on the same Animatable does not run both because a new animation cancels the previous one.

cards.title: Treat Animatable interruption as coroutine cancellation
cards.body: Guidance: An Animatable animation interrupted by animateTo, animateDecay, stop, or snapTo throws CancellationException, so later statements in that caller do not execute normally. Ordinary post-call work runs on a normal return, which can be Finished or BoundReached. Check the returned endReason == Finished before work that requires reaching the target. Limitation: neither interruption nor a normal BoundReached return is successful target completion; a statement after animateTo alone does not distinguish them.

cards.title: Choose stop or snapTo for immediate control
cards.body: Guidance: Use Animatable.stop() to cancel an animation and keep its current value. Use snapTo(value) to cancel it and immediately set the current value and target. Both suspend until the cancellation work completes. Limitation: stop does not jump to the old target, and snapTo clamps the requested value when bounds are configured; both cancel the interrupted animation with CancellationException.

cards.title: Carry decay momentum through AnimationResult
cards.body: Guidance: Feed a fling velocity to Animatable.animateDecay and use its returned AnimationResult.endState.velocity when a following animation should preserve momentum after reaching a bound. Inspect endReason to distinguish Finished from BoundReached. Limitation: Animatable.velocity resets to zero when the animation ends; an externally canceled animation throws CancellationException instead of completing the normal return path.

cards.title: Hand animation control to touch and back to fling
cards.body: Guidance: For custom drag animation, hand control to touch by stopping the ongoing Animatable animation, update drag values with snapTo, and collect samples with VelocityTracker. On release, pass measured velocity to animateDecay for a fling or animateTo the resting position. Launch animation work so gesture handling can continue. Limitation: this is a conceptual handoff, not a production gesture loop. Verify stop placement for each new gesture; immediately stopping a newly launched release animation would cancel the intended fling.

cards.title: Advance the test clock to inspect animation frames
cards.body: Guidance: Disable automatic clock advancement with mainClock.autoAdvance = false before starting the animation, then advanceTimeBy to reach an intermediate state and assert it. ComposeTestRule exposes mainClock so tests can control animation progress deterministically. Limitation: advanceTimeBy rounds the requested duration up to a multiple of the frame duration; do not assume every requested millisecond maps to an exact animation sample.

cards.title: Launch suspend UI responses from event handlers
cards.body: Guidance: Call rememberCoroutineScope in the composable, then launch work from an event callback, such as onClick { scope.launch { snackbarHostState.showSnackbar(message) } }. This also lets event code control or cancel its jobs. Prefer this to storing callback data in MutableState just to trigger LaunchedEffect. Limitation: the scope belongs to the composition call that created it and is cancelled when that call leaves; it is unsuitable for work that must outlive that UI.

cards.title: Keep coroutine launch out of the composable body
cards.body: Guidance: Remembering a CoroutineScope does not make scope.launch safe to call directly while the composable body executes. Launch event-driven jobs inside callbacks; use LaunchedEffect for ongoing jobs initiated by composition. The scope API explicitly prohibits launching jobs into any scope as a side effect of composition itself. Limitation: rememberCoroutineScope retains the scope across recompositions, not the individual launch calls you place in the body.

cards.title: Run UI state animations with a composition coroutine context
cards.body: Guidance: A suspend UI state operation that drives animation can require the MonotonicFrameClock supplied by a composition coroutine context. The official drawer example obtains rememberCoroutineScope in the screen and supplies that context when invoking DrawerState.close from ViewModel-managed logic. Limitation: calling that operation directly in viewModelScope can throw IllegalStateException for a missing frame clock. Hoisting the state to a ViewModel does not supply the required UI coroutine context.

cards.title: Collect Android screen Flows with lifecycle awareness
cards.body: Guidance: For Android UI, collect a Flow as Compose State with collectAsStateWithLifecycle. For its StateFlow overload, StateFlow.value supplies the initial value. Collection starts when the lifecycle reaches minActiveState, stops below it, and restarts on returning; the default threshold is STARTED. Limitation: INITIALIZED is not allowed and throws IllegalArgumentException. Choose the active threshold deliberately; this API controls UI collection, so do not assume every lifecycle state is a valid threshold.

cards.title: Choose collectAsState for platform-agnostic Compose code
cards.body: Guidance: Use collectAsState to convert a Flow to Compose State in platform-agnostic Compose code. It is provided by compose-runtime and does not require the Android lifecycle integration artifact. For Android app screens, the guide recommends lifecycle-aware collectAsStateWithLifecycle instead. Limitation: the two APIs are not interchangeable lifecycle policies; the guide identifies collectAsStateWithLifecycle as the lifecycle-aware option.

cards.title: Audit effect inputs for restart versus latest-value behavior
cards.body: Guidance: Review each value used inside an effect: make it a key when changes must cancel and restart the work; use rememberUpdatedState when the running work must read its latest value without restarting. Apply this review to produceState and DisposableEffect too. A lifecycle owner must be a DisposableEffect key so replacing it moves the observer to the new owner. Limitation: omitting a restart input can leave work bound to an old object; adding needless restart keys can repeatedly cancel useful work.

cards.title: Keep snapshotFlow observation blocks pure and read-only
cards.body: Guidance: Use the snapshotFlow block only to read snapshot state and calculate a result. It runs in a read-only Snapshot: modifying snapshot data inside it makes collection fail with IllegalStateException. Keep the block idempotent and free of side effects because it may run repeatedly for equal inputs or once after many rapid changes. Limitation: it cannot serve as an exactly-once event-processing block; observable state can lose intermediate events, and block execution does not promise one run per change.

cards.title: Let callers own the lifetime of suspend work
cards.body: Guidance: Expose one-shot data or business operations as suspend functions and ongoing changes as Flow so the caller controls execution, lifetime, and cancellation. If such an operation needs parallel child work relevant only to the current screen, use coroutineScope or supervisorScope inside the suspend operation rather than detaching the work. Limitation: work that must outlive the caller needs an explicitly managed longer-lived external scope; the current screen lifetime is not suitable for that requirement.

cards.title: Make long-running coroutine work check cancellation
cards.body: Guidance: Coroutine cancellation is cooperative: a cancelled Job takes effect when work suspends or checks cancellation. In a loop that performs blocking operations, call ensureActive before each unit of work, as in the guide's file-reading example. The guide notes that kotlinx.coroutines suspend functions such as delay and withContext are cancellable. Limitation: merely cancelling the Job does not add cancellation checks inside your blocking work; ensure it reaches a check or cancellable suspension point.

cards.title: Rethrow cancellation exceptions after local handling
cards.body: Guidance: Treat CancellationException as coroutine cancellation. If you must catch it for local handling, rethrow it so cancellation propagates through the coroutine hierarchy, for example catch (e: CancellationException) { throw e }. Limitation: catching and swallowing this exception can break cancellation propagation; a catch block must not turn cancellation into a successful operation result.

cards.title: Expose one modifier as the first optional parameter
cards.body: Guidance: A reusable Compose UI element should accept one Modifier parameter named modifier as its first optional parameter. Keep required data and event parameters before it, and avoid multiple Modifier parameters on the element API. Review this public signature separately from internal modifier ordering. Limitation: this guideline addresses Compose UI element functions; it does not establish the API contract of every helper composable.

cards.title: Reserve CompositionLocal for tree-scoped dependencies with usable defaults
cards.body: Guidance: Use CompositionLocal for dependencies that can reasonably be needed by any descendant of a UI subtree, such as design-system context. Give the local a useful default; if no default is possible, make omission of its provider exceedingly difficult. This keeps previews and focused component tests practical. Pass a component only the state and events it needs instead of hiding a screen ViewModel in a local. Limitation: convenient access alone does not justify a local when only a few descendants need the dependency.

cards.title: Choose local creation by change frequency and invalidation scope
cards.body: Guidance: compositionLocalOf tracks current-value reads; changing its provided value invalidates those readers. staticCompositionLocalOf does not track those reads; changing its provided value recomposes the entire provider content. Prefer staticCompositionLocalOf for values highly unlikely to change, and account for broader invalidation when that assumption changes. Limitation: static is not a general optimization for every theme value; choose using the actual provider update behavior.

cards.title: Choose an explicit boundary for extending or replacing a theme
cards.body: Guidance: Choose whether a custom design system extends MaterialTheme with additional values, replaces selected color, typography, or shape systems while retaining others, or replaces MaterialTheme entirely. Document that boundary before reviewing reused Material components, because their integration depends on the chosen approach. Limitation: these are supported design-system alternatives, not a requirement that a custom system adopt Material tokens or component behavior.

cards.title: Adapt component defaults to the active custom theme
cards.body: Guidance: When reusing Material components without MaterialTheme, wrap them and explicitly supply the custom color, typography, shape, and other system values they need; expose other intended options as parameters. Prefer values from the custom theme. The guide example passes custom colors and shape to Button and supplies its content typography with ProvideTextStyle. Limitation: a custom theme accessor alone does not redirect Material defaults. New value types such as gradients may make a fresh component implementation more suitable than a wrapper.

cards.title: Share interaction ownership and pair press completion events
cards.body: Guidance: If component input, observers, and a custom indication need one interaction stream, route them through the same MutableInteractionSource. A custom IndicationNodeFactory receives an InteractionSource, and clickable can integrate the indication. When manually producing press events, retain the original Press and reference it from the matching Release or Cancel; completion events identify their starting interaction. Limitation: low-level interactions do not interpret a click action. The guide also permits a null source when callers do not need an exposed stream.

cards.title: Keep ModifierNodeElement updates consistent with node reuse
cards.body: Guidance: Keep ModifierNodeElement immutable and use it to create or update a reusable modifier node. create instantiates the node when the modifier is first applied. When the element changes at the same position, update must copy the current inputs into the existing node rather than create another node. Implement equals and hashCode consistently: update is triggered when equality with the previous element is false. Limitation: checking this configuration contract does not verify attachment, detachment, or resource cleanup behavior.

cards.title: Measure children once within incoming constraints
cards.body: Guidance: In a custom Layout, use the parent's minimum and maximum width and height constraints when choosing the layout size. Measure children, decide the parent size, then place the measured children. Measure each child only once; measuring twice throws a runtime exception. If sizing needs information before measurement, query intrinsics rather than measuring a child a second time. Limitation: this describes ordinary Compose layout; it does not specify a custom layout's constraint propagation or intrinsic formula.

cards.title: Match custom intrinsic measurements to the measure policy
cards.body: Guidance: A custom Layout or layout modifier gets approximate intrinsic measurements by default; those approximations can be wrong for its layout algorithm. Override minIntrinsicWidth, minIntrinsicHeight, maxIntrinsicWidth, or maxIntrinsicHeight on MeasurePolicy when needed, keeping each answer consistent with measure. For a column that gives every child the full width, minimum intrinsic height for that width is the sum of child minimum intrinsic heights. Limitation: the column formula is not a general formula for other layouts.

cards.title: Choose relative or absolute placement deliberately for RTL
cards.body: Guidance: For manual placement in a Layout or layout modifier, MeasureScope.layoutDirection exposes the current direction. placeRelative changes placement with left-to-right versus right-to-left direction; place uses absolute coordinates. When calculating direction-dependent coordinates yourself, use place so placement does not apply another direction-dependent change. LocalLayoutDirection can change the direction of a composable. Limitation: this guidance does not define a component's visual mirroring policy; check both directions for its intended arrangement.

cards.title: Reserve layout space for minimum touch targets
cards.body: Guidance: Give interactive elements a minimum 48 dp size for the Material accessibility guideline, for example Modifier.sizeIn(minWidth = 48.dp, minHeight = 48.dp). Compose can expand a small clickable element's touch target outside its visible bounds; allocate enough layout space to avoid overlapping neighboring touch areas. Material 3 minimumInteractiveComponentSize reserves layout space for a smaller visual element; it does not itself expand the touch target. Limitation: a preceding size modifier can limit the reserved space; verify the final hit areas in the consuming layout.

cards.title: Remember and connect a focus requester before requesting focus
cards.body: Guidance: Remember a FocusRequester and connect it through Modifier.focusRequester. Request focus in response to an event rather than directly during composition. In the captured source, requestFocus(focusDirection = FocusDirection.Enter) returns a Boolean reporting success or cancellation; a request does not guarantee that focus moved. Limitation: check the overload available in the resolved project version. These excerpts do not establish software keyboard visibility, accessibility focus, or custom-control modifier ordering.

cards.title: Expose complex gestures as labeled accessibility actions
cards.body: Guidance: Expose a complex gesture such as swipe to dismiss through semantics.customActions with a descriptive CustomAccessibilityAction label and the same operation in its action callback. Custom actions can also move repeated child operations into a container's action menu. When moving those operations, clear the original child semantics to avoid keeping duplicate traversal targets. Limitation: only clear child semantics when their actions have been represented on the container; verify the resulting action menu and traversal with assistive technology.

cards.title: Supply the frame clock used by finite animation dispatch
cards.body: Guidance: Finite animation frame dispatch calls withFrameNanos. That function uses the calling CoroutineContext's MonotonicFrameClock and throws IllegalStateException if the clock is absent. Keep frame-driven UI animation in a context that supplies the appropriate local frame clock. Limitation: a dispatcher selects where work runs; it does not by itself supply this frame clock. This is a requirement of the frame-dispatch path, not of every suspend function.

cards.title: Honor the Stable annotation contract before overriding inference
cards.body: Guidance: Annotate a class or interface @Stable only when equals gives a consistent result for the same two instances, composition is notified when a public property changes, and all public property types are stable. The annotation communicates guarantees to the compiler; it does not implement change notification. Limitation: violating these assumptions has undefined behavior. Overriding stability inference can suppress expected recomposition, and annotating collection-heavy models can replace cheap identity checks with expensive structural equals checks under strong skipping.

cards.title: Account for identity and object equality under strong skipping
cards.body: Guidance: With strong skipping enabled, restartable composables can be skipped even when parameters are unstable. Compose compares unstable parameters by instance equality (===) and stable parameters by Object.equals(); unchanged parameters allow skipping. Limitation: do not assume that equal field values make two newly allocated unstable instances equal for skipping. Non-restartable composables remain unskippable. Check the project's actual compiler configuration before applying this behavior; the application's compiler version and settings are unknown here.

cards.title: Cache expensive calculations using their actual inputs
cards.body: Guidance: Cache an expensive repeatable calculation with remember and key it by the inputs used, for example remember(contacts, comparator) { contacts.sortedWith(comparator) }. The calculation runs initially and is regenerated when those inputs change. remember stores its keys and compares them using Object.equals() on recomposition. Limitation: caching is useful for costly calculations, heavy allocations, or required object identity; it is not free work and does not make the initial calculation asynchronous.

cards.title: Exercise saveable state restoration with StateRestorationTester
cards.body: Guidance: Wrap the test content in StateRestorationTester(composeTestRule).setContent, perform actions that change saveable UI state, call emulateSavedInstanceStateRestore(), and assert that the state was restored. This targets rememberSaveable restoration without requiring activity recreation. Limitation: the tester simulates recreation of a composable; this check alone does not establish that the entire activity or application survives actual process recreation.

cards.title: Reuse lazy compositions within the same content type
cards.body: For heterogeneous lazy lists or grids, provide contentType based on the item structure. Compose can reuse compositions between items of the same type instead of attempting reuse across different structures. The official guide recommends this for composition reuse; it does not establish a measured speedup for your app. This card covers reuse grouping, not item identity or saved-state behavior. Validate performance in the target app; released-version applicability remains unknown.

cards.title: Give asynchronously loaded lazy items a useful initial size
cards.body: Give lazy items that load images or other data asynchronously a nonzero default size. Zero-height items can all fit in the first measurement, causing unnecessary composition before loaded content expands. When the eventual size is approximately known, keep placeholder and loaded sizes consistent to help maintain scroll position. Choose dimensions appropriate to the content rather than treating the guide example as a universal size. Released-version applicability remains unknown.
